key_insight: Machine-learned dynamics reveal that small polarons at oxygen-deficient TiO2(110) surfaces move orders of magnitude more slowly than in bulk because surface hopping pathways are strongly restricted.
engineering_relevance: The results help explain why porous rutile TiO2 shows lower electron mobility than single-crystal material and inform defect/surface engineering for catalysis and energy devices.
method: Extended machine-learning-assisted polaron dynamics to a reducible oxide surface.
Ran nanosecond-scale finite-temperature dynamics on oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110).
Compared surface and bulk polaron hopping pathways and mobility.
evidence_signal: The study uses several nanoseconds of temperature-dependent dynamics, showing surface polaron mobility is suppressed by several orders of magnitude versus bulk and that vacancies bias electron localization near Ti sites.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate transferable ML dynamics for defect-rich surface environments, so generalization to other oxides and defect chemistries should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Machine-learned dynamics of surface polarons at reduced oxide surfaces
